meta.title: Who really said "Education is a weapon whose effects depend on who holds it in his hands and at whom it is aimed"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Yes, Stalin said it, to H. G. Wells on 23 July 1934. The popular English closely follows his Russian; the standard translation words it differently.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Education is a weapon whose effects depend on who holds it in his hands and at whom it is aimed'?
meta.ogDescription: Yes, Stalin said it, to H. G. Wells on 23 July 1934. The popular English closely follows his Russian; the standard translation words it differently.

answer.label: Spoken by
answer.sourceLine: Stalin said it in Russian, in his conversation with H. G. Wells dated 23 July 1934: “Ведь образование — это оружие, эффект которого зависит от того, кто его держит в своих руках, кого этим оружием хотят ударить.” The popular English follows that sentence almost word for word, but its translator is unidentified. The standard English text of the interview words it differently.

source.heading: Where Stalin said it

docMeta.dd: Conversation with the English writer H. G. Wells (English title: “Marxism Versus Liberalism”)
Bol’shevik, 1934, no. 17 (as reproduced in Stalin’s collected works, vol. 14)
Popular wording: unidentified translator, a close literal rendering of the Russian. Standard English: Works, Vol. 14 (London: Red Star Press, 1978)

source.excerpt: Just now you spoke about “educated people.” But what educated people did you have in mind? Were there not plenty of educated people on the side of the old order in England in the seventeenth century, in France at the end of the eighteenth century, and in Russia in the epoch of the October Revolution? The old order had in its service many highly educated people who defended the old order, who opposed the new order. Education is a weapon the effect of which is determined by the hands which wield it, by who is to be struck down.
trail: 23 July 1934: Stalin talks with H. G. Wells. The Russian transcript, printed in Bol’shevik (1934, no. 17), has the sentence “образование — это оружие, эффект которого зависит от того, кто его держит в своих руках…” (Russian text, Marxists Internet Archive ↗)

Standard English: the English text in Stalin’s Works, Vol. 14 (Red Star Press, London, 1978) reads “Education is a weapon the effect of which is determined by the hands which wield it, by who is to be struck down” (English text ↗)

The popular wording, “whose effects depend on who holds it in his hands and at whom it is aimed,” is what quote collections repeat. Wikiquote lists it under Stalin’s interviews but gives the source as “Interview with H. G. Wells (September 1937)” (Wikiquote ↗)
Mis-dated: a library blog prints the line as “Joseph Stalin, 1953” and cites J. B. Simpson’s Contemporary Quotations (1964) (USF Gleeson Library blog ↗)
source.excerptNote: Standard English text from Works, Vol. 14 (Red Star Press, 1978). The Russian original reads: “Ведь образование — это оружие, эффект которого зависит от того, кто его держит в своих руках, кого этим оружием хотят ударить.” Literally: “After all, education is a weapon whose effect depends on who holds it in his hands, whom one wants to strike with this weapon.” The popular quotation is close to that literal reading.

source.rightsNote: The words are Stalin’s, from a Russian transcript published in 1934. The popular English wording comes from a translation we could not identify, so we assert no copyright status for it. The different standard English text appears in Works, Vol. 14 (Red Star Press, 1978), which the Marxists Internet Archive transcribes.

author.name: Joseph Stalin
author.heading: About Joseph Stalin
author.metaLine: 1878–1953 · Soviet leader, General Secretary of the Communist Party
author.bio: Born Ioseb Jughashvili in Georgia, Joseph Stalin rose through the Bolshevik party and led the Soviet Union from the 1920s until his death in 1953. His rule combined forced industrialization and collectivization with mass repression. In July 1934 he gave the English novelist H. G. Wells a long interview that was widely published and debated in the West.

misattribution.heading: The real story: right speaker, loose wording, wrong dates
misattribution.intro: This is one of the rare viral Stalin quotations that he actually said. What goes wrong online is the wording and the date.

items.why: Stalin’s standard English text does not say “whose effects depend on who holds it in his hands and at whom it is aimed.” Works, Vol. 14 gives “Education is a weapon the effect of which is determined by the hands which wield it, by who is to be struck down” (English text ↗). The popular version is closer to the Russian original ↗, but no one has identified who translated it.
Wikiquote’s source note reads “Interview with H. G. Wells (September 1937)” (Wikiquote ↗). The transcript of the conversation is dated 23 July 1934 (MIA ↗).
Some citations print the line as “Joseph Stalin, 1953,” for example a library blog that cites Simpson’s Contemporary Quotations (1964) (USF blog ↗). The words come from the 1934 Wells conversation.

misattribution.truthLine: Joseph Stalin said it, in Russian, to H. G. Wells on 23 July 1934. The viral English is a fair but unofficial translation of his sentence (Russian text ↗).

context.heading: Why he said it
lead: Wells, then president of the PEN writers’ club, came to Moscow to ask Stalin “what you are doing to change the world.” He argued that class-war propaganda “may detach from socialism just those educated people whom socialism needs.”

Stalin turned the point around. Educated people had served the old order in seventeenth-century England, eighteenth-century France and Russia in 1917. Education, he said, is a weapon, and what it does depends on whose side it serves. He went on to say that the proletariat does need highly educated people, and that the real question is “which intelligentsia” is meant.
context.detailsSummary: How the Russian sentence compares with the two English versions
detailsBody: Russian: “Ведь образование — это оружие, эффект которого зависит от того, кто его держит в своих руках, кого этим оружием хотят ударить.”
Standard English (Works, Vol. 14): “Education is a weapon the effect of which is determined by the hands which wield it, by who is to be struck down.”

Popular English: “Education is a weapon whose effects depend on who holds it in his hands and at whom it is aimed.” “Who holds it in his hands” matches the Russian word for word. “At whom it is aimed” loosens the Russian, which literally says “whom one wants to strike with this weapon.”

sourcesVerified.claim: The English text of Stalin's interview with H. G. Wells, dated 23 July 1934 and sourced to Works, Vol. 14 (Red Star Press, London, 1978), has Stalin say: 'Education is a weapon the effect of which is determined by the hands which wield it, by who is to be struck down.' The same page has Wells's 'class war propaganda may detach from socialism just those educated people whom socialism needs' and his PEN presidency.

The Russian text 'Беседа с английским писателем Г.Д. Уэллсом 23 июля 1934 года' contains 'Ведь образование– это оружие, эффект которого зависит от того, кто его держит в своих руках, кого этим оружием хотят ударить' and ends with the source note 'Большевик. 1934. № 17.'

Wikiquote lists 'Education is a weapon whose effects depend on who holds it in his hands and at whom it is aimed.' under Stalin's speeches, writings and interviews, with the source note 'Interview with H. G. Wells (September 1937)'.
A USF Gleeson Library blog prints the line as 'Joseph Stalin, 1953' and cites Simpson, J. B. (1964), Contemporary Quotations (New York: Crowell).
The New Statesman says that in 1934 H. G. Wells interviewed Joseph Stalin in Moscow, and that the interview and the debate that followed appeared in the magazine.
